extracted.intended_audience: web developers and authors integrating MathJax who need accessibility/assistive-technology support
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation on MathJax v4 accessibility components and how to enable/configure them for assistive technology (screen readers, keyboard exploration, collapsing complex expressions). Covers component purposes, loading, defaults, and migration notes from earlier MathJax versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading assistive components via loader.load
rubrics_metrics.description: To load one of these components, include the component name in the load array of the loader block of your MathJax configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example configuration: MathJax={ loader:{ load: ['a11y/semantic-enrich'] } }. Use the loader.load array to explicitly include any a11y component you require in your MathJax setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined components include common assistive extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The semantic-enrich, speech, and explorer components are part of all the combined components, so if you are using one of those, you don’t need to load these assistive extensions yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use one of MathJax's combined builds, these assistive components are already bundled; avoid redundant explicit loading. This reduces configuration complexity for typical deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Menu-driven dynamic loading of assistive extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not using a combined component, but are using the ui/menu component, there are menu items that will cause these assistive extensions to be loaded dynamically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the MathJax contextual menu lets page authors defer loading assistive extensions until a user requests them, so explicit loader configuration is not strictly necessary when the menu UI is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: a11y/semantic-enrich: semantic enrichment and structure attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: The semantic-enrich component connects MathJax with the Speech Rule Engine, which allows MathJax to analyze the mathematics that it processes and add attributes that represent the semantic structure of the mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic enrichment may modify the underlying MathML for each expression to better represent structure, improving line-breaking and speech generation. See the Semantic-Enrich Extension Options for configuration details.

rubrics_metrics.name: a11y/speech: speech-string generation for math
rubrics_metrics.description: The speech component connects MathJax with the Speech Rule Engine, which allows MathJax to generate speech strings for the mathematics that it processes. These can be attached to the output for use by screen readers, or for use with the a11y/explorer component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The speech component performs speech computations in web-workers (separate threads) so it does not interfere with page responsiveness or slow typesetting. See the Speech Extension Options for configuration. Use this when you need explicit speech output or to support AT that consumes speech strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: a11y/explorer: interactive keyboard exploration of expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: The explorer component allows readers to explore a mathematical expression interactively. When an expression is focused by tabbing to it, the expression can be explored using the arrow keys; clicking on a typeset expression will also enter the explorer at the character that is clicked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keyboard navigation: down moves to more detail by selecting the first subexpression, up moves to more complete expressions, left and right move through sub-expressions at the current level. The explorer integrates with speech output and is the default assistive tool in v4; see Explorer Extension Options for configuration and further accessibility features.

rubrics_metrics.name: a11y/complexity: compute complexity and collapse complex subexpressions
rubrics_metrics.description: The complexity component computes a complexity measure for each element within an expression, and allows complex expressions to “collapse” to make them both shorter and simpler to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collapsed portions can be expanded with a mouse click or keyboard actions when using the a11y/explorer extension. Configure complexity thresholds and behavior via the Complexity Extension Options.

rubrics_metrics.name: a11y/assistive-mml: embed hidden MathML for MathML-enabled screen readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The assistive-mml component embeds visually hidden MathML alongside MathJax’s visual rendering while hiding the visual rendering from assistive technology (AT) such as screenreaders. This allows most MathML-enabled screenreaders to read out the underlying mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation MathML is not expressive enough to voice mathematics properly in all circumstances; screenreaders rely on heuristics to semantically analyze the MathML. In v2/v3 assistive-mml was enabled by default; in v4 the explorer is the default assistive tool but assistive-mml can be re-enabled via the contextual menu or configuration. See the Assistive-MML Extension Options and Screen Reader Support sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech Rule Engine dependency and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Several accessibility components (semantic-enrich and speech) connect MathJax with the Speech Rule Engine to analyze math and produce semantic attributes or speech strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because speech rule computations can be time-consuming, the speech component uses web-workers to offload computation and avoid slowing page rendering. Configure engine options in the respective extension option sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version/migration notes for assistive features (v2/v3 → v4)
rubrics_metrics.description: In v3, the semantic-enrich extension included both semantic enrichment and speech generation; in v4 these functions are accomplished by two distinct extensions with speech split into its own extension. The assistive-mml extension was loaded and enabled by default in v2 and v3, but in v4 the explorer component has replaced it as the default assistive tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of renamed/split functionality and default changes when upgrading to v4. The auto-collapse extension from v2 has not yet been converted to v4 (planned for a future release). The assistive-menu extension from v2 is now part of the standard contextual menu extension and need not be loaded separately.
